title: Supervisor and specialized agents
content: A supervisor decomposes a request, delegates bounded tasks to specialized agents, receives their results, and chooses the next action. Keeping the supervisor in the loop makes ownership and control flow explicit.

title: Shared state and communication
content: A shared state object carries the user request, intermediate research, retrieved documents, analysis, validation, errors, and final response between agents. Agents communicate by returning structured results to the supervisor.

title: Coordination costs and failure modes
content: Multiple agents can add latency, duplicated work, conflicting conclusions, and more failure points. Clear task ownership, bounded delegation, validation, and observable handoffs help manage those costs.

title: When a single agent becomes difficult to scale
content: A single agent that plans, retrieves, reasons, validates, and writes can accumulate a large prompt and tangled responsibilities. Complex tasks are harder to debug, parallelize, and verify when intermediate ownership is implicit.
